title: Australian police arrest two over TeamPCP hacks targeting Mercor, OpenAI, and others
slides: Arrested, but who else stays free?

thread_text:
1. Who else stays free?

Police tied the duo to TeamPCP attacks, but the chatter suggests more actors were involved.

2. Targets beyond OpenAI

Mercor, OpenAI, and others were hit — each breach exposes a different kind of sensitive data.

3. Data may already be out

Your credentials, financial records, or internal memos could be circulating in private channels right now.

4. The twist: access logs

Investigators found the trail through overlooked access logs — the same logs you may not be checking.

5. Audit today

Open your access logs and look for unusual logins or data exports before tomorrow. If you find none, set up alerts.

instagram.caption:
Two people got arrested for breaking into OpenAI and Mercor — but the police say the chatter points to more people still out there.

The duo allegedly worked with a group called TeamPCP. They hit at least two companies you’ve heard of, plus others you haven't. Each breach exposed different data: login credentials, financial records, internal files.

If you've ever used those platforms, your info might be in private channels right now. The trail was found through access logs — the same logs most teams ignore.

Open your access logs today and look for logins you don't recognize or data exports after midnight. If nothing looks off, set up alerts so you're not the last to know next time.

Do you actually know who has access to your accounts right now? 🔐📂🧾
